In a second-price-style auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Setting the sealed bid equal to my value ensures I win exactly when the second-highest bid is below my value and pay that second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. Overbidding risks negative payoff if I win at a price above my value; underbidding risks missing profitable wins. With value $20 and no informative history, bid truthfully at 20.

[ This is a second-price mechanism: the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid (the exit of the second-to-last bidder). The dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit; shading only lowers win probability without reducing price conditional on winning. With one round and no history to exploit, I should set my sealed bid equal to my value ($20) to win when competitors’ top value is below 20 and pay that amount; otherwise I lose with zero payoff. Never overbid to avoid negative surplus. ]
